title: Tool return text sent to the model changes after a message history round trip (datetime, UUID, Decimal, bytes, str Enum)

comments.body:
<!-- pydanty:status-comment:v1 -->
**Decision:** maintainer discussion

The drift is real on current main and violates the checked-in prompt-prefix-stability guarantee; the remedy is a **maintainer decision**: preserve each value's JSON encoding through the round trip, or send these scalars unquoted from the start — which changes first-run prompts.

**Why it matters:** Any app that saves and resumes message history — the documented pattern — sends a changed prompt after restore, so provider prompt caches miss and replays differ from the original run.

**Evidence:** - **Reproduced:** `datetime`/`date`/`UUID`/`Decimal`/`bytes` tool returns go quoted → unquoted after the documented save/restore (https://play.pydantic.work/p/FkNMx2FB); str-valued Enums do not drift.
- **Cause:** `model_response_str` passes `str` content through and JSON-encodes everything else: `pydantic_ai_slim/pydantic_ai/messages.py:1609-1615`.

  https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/blob/69ea1e57201ed59e7d30fbe4a7590d193acecce0/pydantic_ai_slim/pydantic_ai/messages.py#L1609-L1615

- **Related:** the `bytes` slice is tracked in https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/issues/8367; no statement decides scalar quoting.

title: [Question/Design] Make Trial serializable with cloudpickle

comments.body:
Thanks for raising this!

It seems that making `Trial` serializable would require separating its state from runtime dependencies (e.g., storage references or internal context). One possible approach could be to introduce a lightweight, serializable representation of `Trial` that only contains essential attributes, while keeping non-serializable parts on the worker side.

However, this might introduce tradeoffs such as:
- Increased complexity in maintaining consistency between serialized and live objects
- Potential performance overhead during serialization/deserialization
- Risk of breaking existing APIs or assumptions

Would it make sense to explore a minimal “proxy” or “snapshot” version of Trial for remote callbacks instead of fully serializing the object?

title: [BUG] `strands`, `semantic_kernel` and `haystack` autolog export every span twice when `MLFLOW_USE_DEFAULT_TRACER_PROVIDER=false`

comments.body:
<!-- mlflow-triage-run:38004163876 -->

> [!NOTE]
> [Automated triage](https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow/actions/runs/38004163876/attempts/1). Please verify the findings.

### Summary

**Reproduced**: with `MLFLOW_USE_DEFAULT_TRACER_PROVIDER=false`, `mlflow.strands.autolog()` makes MLflow export every span on the shared provider twice. This includes non-Strands spans such as `mlflow.start_span()`. It happens at `master` (0a881c2). In isolated mode each span is exported once.

- Expected: each span reaches `MlflowV3SpanExporter.export` once in both tracer-provider modes.
- Actual: shared mode gives `total exports=8  unique spans=4  ratio=2.0`. If a span is started before `autolog()`, it gives `ratio=1.5`.
- Fails at: [`mlflow/strands/autolog.py#L84-L85`](https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow/blob/0a881c229f6aa5118fd5322f28d2b99f183ad235/mlflow/strands/autolog.py#L84-L85) (and the `on_start` forward at [L55](https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow/blob/0a881c229f6aa5118fd5322f28d2b99f183ad235/mlflow/strands/autolog.py#L55))

### How to reproduce

Tested on MLflow `master` @ 0a881c2, Python 3.10.22, Linux, with strands-agents 1.57.2 and opentelemetry-sdk 1.45.0.

I used the issue's `repro_strands_double_export.py` unchanged:

```shell
uv run --with strands-agents python repro_strands_double_export.py shared
#   exported 2x  chat / execute_event_loop_cycle / invoke_agent example-agent / manual-span
#   total exports=8  unique spans=4  ratio=2.0
uv run --with strands-agents python repro_strands_double_export.py isolated
#   total exports=4  unique spans=4  ratio=1.0
```

For the warm-up variant from "Other info" #2, I added a `mlflow.start_span("warmup")` and `export_counts.clear()` before `autolog()`. That gives `total exports=6  unique spans=4  ratio=1.5` in shared mode.

### Suggested fix

The root cause matches the issue's analysis. In shared mode, [`provider.py#L666-L679`](https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow/blob/0a881c229f6aa5118fd5322f28d2b99f183ad235/mlflow/tracing/provider.py#L666-L679) adds MLflow's processors to the global `SynchronousMultiSpanProcessor`, which already holds `StrandsSpanProcessor`. So `_get_tracer(__name__).span_processor` is that same composite. The re-entrancy guard from #20809 stops the recursion, but the forward still runs MLflow's processor, and the composite then runs it again in its own loop.

Below is the minimal patch I verified. It changes only `mlflow/strands/autolog.py`:

```diff
@@ def on_start(self, span, parent_context=None):
-            tracer = _get_tracer(__name__)
+            processors_before = _get_span_processors(get_tracer_provider())
+            tracer = _get_tracer(__name__)
             if isinstance(tracer, NoOpTracer):
                 return
-
-            tracer.span_processor.on_start(span, parent_context)
+            # Shared provider: the dispatching composite already runs MLflow's processors,
+            # unless _get_tracer() just registered them (the in-progress loop won't reach them).
+            processors = _get_span_processors(tracer)
+            if self not in processors or processors != processors_before:
+                tracer.span_processor.on_start(span, parent_context)
@@ def on_end(self, span):
             tracer = _get_tracer(__name__)
-            tracer.span_processor.on_end(span)
+            if self not in _get_span_processors(tracer):
+                tracer.span_processor.on_end(span)
@@
+def _get_span_processors(tracer_or_provider) -> tuple[object, ...]:
+    composite = getattr(tracer_or_provider, "span_processor", None) or getattr(
+        tracer_or_provider, "_active_span_processor", None
+    )
+    return getattr(composite, "_span_processors", ())
+
 def setup_strands_tracing():
@@
-            provider.add_span_processor(processor)
+            # Run first so on_end enriches spans before MLflow's processor exports them.
+            provider._active_span_processor._span_processors = (
+                processor,
+                *provider._active_span_processor._span_processors,
+            )
```

With this patch:

- Both the plain repro and the warm-up variant give `ratio=1.0` in shared and isolated modes.
- The enriched span types are kept (`AGENT`, `CHAT_MODEL`).
- `uv run --with strands-agents pytest tests/strands` passes (7 tests).

This matches the fix the reporter described. A regression test should count exports per span, which `test_strands_autolog_shared_provider_no_recursion` does not do. `SemanticKernelSpanProcessor` and `HaystackSpanProcessor` forward the same way, so they likely need the same change. I did not verify those two.

Thanks for the triage run and the independent reproduction.

After the run, I updated the description to cover two more autologgers. `mlflow.semantic_kernel.autolog()` and `mlflow.haystack.autolog()` have the same bug: `SemanticKernelSpanProcessor` and `HaystackSpanProcessor` received the same guard in #20809 and forward the same way, and in shared mode they export every span twice. The reproduction and results are in "Other info", section 4. The fix branch now covers all three: [compare with `master`](https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow/compare/master...LeviLong01:mlflow:ll/fix-autolog-shared-provider-double-export).

The fix and a regression tests are ready on my fork, and I'll open a PR as soon as a maintainer marks this issue `ready`:[compare with `master`](https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow/compare/master...LeviLong01:mlflow:ll/fix-autolog-shared-provider-double-export)

title: [BUG] Async logging (`synchronous=False`) applies writes for the same run out of order

comments.body:
<!-- mlflow-triage-run:37941007226 -->

> [!NOTE]
> [Automated triage](https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow/actions/runs/37941007226/attempts/1). Please verify the findings.

### Summary

**Reproduced**: with `synchronous=False`, batches for the same run go to a 10-worker thread pool and can be applied out of order, so the last-logged value often isn't the one that gets stored. Reproduced at current master (`3.17.1.dev0`).

- Expected: `wrong final tag in 0/10 runs`
- Actual: `wrong final tag in 10/10 runs` (`0/10` with `MLFLOW_ASYNC_LOGGING_THREADPOOL_SIZE=1`)
- Fails at: https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow/blob/6a5bd6c174dcdec4f3f7f0b63962637685fe76f0/mlflow/utils/async_logging/async_logging_queue.py#L211-L213

### How to reproduce

Tested on MLflow 3.17.1.dev0 (6a5bd6c), Python 3.10.22, Linux.

```python
import tempfile
import mlflow

mlflow.set_tracking_uri(f"sqlite:///{tempfile.mkdtemp()}/m.db")
wrong = 0
for _ in range(10):
    with mlflow.start_run() as run:
        for i in range(20):
            mlflow.set_tag("stage", str(i), synchronous=False)
    wrong += mlflow.get_run(run.info.run_id).data.tags["stage"] != "19"
print(f"wrong final tag in {wrong}/10 runs")
```

```
$ uv run python repro.py
wrong final tag in 10/10 runs
$ MLFLOW_ASYNC_LOGGING_THREADPOOL_SIZE=1 uv run python repro.py
wrong final tag in 0/10 runs
```

### Suggested fix

`_log_run_data` dequeues batches in FIFO order, but [submits each one to `_batch_logging_worker_threadpool` on its own](https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow/blob/6a5bd6c174dcdec4f3f7f0b63962637685fe76f0/mlflow/utils/async_logging/async_logging_queue.py#L197-L222). That pool has `MLFLOW_ASYNC_LOGGING_THREADPOOL_SIZE or 10` workers ([L337-L340](https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow/blob/6a5bd6c174dcdec4f3f7f0b63962637685fe76f0/mlflow/utils/async_logging/async_logging_queue.py#L337-L340)), so nothing keeps two batches for the same run in order.

The fix: keep a per-run FIFO, and run at most one drain task per run, so different runs still log concurrently. Core of the change:

```diff
+        self._run_queues: dict[str, deque[RunBatch]] = {}
+        self._run_queues_lock = threading.Lock()
 ...
         for run_batch in run_batches:
+            with self._run_queues_lock:
+                run_queue = self._run_queues.setdefault(run_batch.run_id, deque())
+                run_queue.append(run_batch)
+                if len(run_queue) > 1:
+                    # A worker is already draining this run's queue.
+                    continue
             try:
-                self._batch_logging_worker_threadpool.submit(logging_func, run_batch)
+                self._batch_logging_worker_threadpool.submit(
+                    self._drain_run_queue, run_batch.run_id
+                )
             except Exception as e:
                 ...
+                with self._run_queues_lock:
+                    del self._run_queues[run_batch.run_id]
                 run_batch.exception = e
                 run_batch.complete()
+
+    def _drain_run_queue(self, run_id: str) -> None:
+        while True:
+            with self._run_queues_lock:
+                run_batch = self._run_queues[run_id][0]
+            # existing logging_func body: call self._logging_func, set exception, complete()
+            ...
+            with self._run_queues_lock:
+                run_queue = self._run_queues[run_id]
+                run_queue.popleft()
+                if not run_queue:
+                    del self._run_queues[run_id]
+                    return
```

Also remove `_run_queues` and `_run_queues_lock` in `__getstate__`, and recreate them in `__setstate__`.

Checked with this patch applied:
- The repro prints `wrong final tag in 0/10 runs`.
- `tests/utils/test_async_logging_queue.py` and `tests/utils/test_async_artifacts_logging_queue.py` pass (13 tests).
- The async tests selected from `tests/tracking/test_tracking.py` and `tests/tracking/test_client.py` pass.

One assertion needs updating. [`test_single_thread_publish_consume_queue`](https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow/blob/6a5bd6c174dcdec4f3f7f0b63962637685fe76f0/tests/utils/test_async_logging_queue.py#L83-L84) mocks `submit` and expects 2 calls. Both grouped batches belong to the same run, so the patch submits only once (`call_count == 1`). A regression test like the repro above (many `set_tag` calls on one run, check the final value) should go with the fix.

title: Compatible api_version ranges reject untagged base images with registry ports

comments.body:
I reproduced this on current `main` (`cba111d`) using the reporter's example verbatim, and it fails exactly as described with `click.UsageError: Compatible api_version ranges cannot be used with a tagged base_image.`

**Root cause**

`_ensure_compatible_api_version_base_image` in `libs/cli/langgraph_cli/config.py` treats any colon in the reference as a tag separator:

```python
if ":" in base_image:
    raise click.UsageError(...)
```

In a Docker image reference a tag can only appear in the final `name[:tag]` segment after the last `/`. A colon before that belongs to a registry `host:port`, so `registry.example.com:5000/team/langgraph-api` is untagged but still rejected. `localhost:5000/langgraph-api` hits the same path.

**Proposed fix**

Narrow the check to the segment that can actually carry a tag:

```python
last_segment = base_image.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
if ":" in last_segment:
    raise click.UsageError(...)
```

This keeps rejecting tagged images, including tagged images on a port-qualified registry (`registry.example.com:5000/team/langgraph-api:0.11.0`), since the tag is still in the last segment.

**Validation so far**

With that change, the reporter's example produces the expected `registry.example.com:5000/team/langgraph-api:0.11.1-py3.11`. I added three regression tests next to the existing `test_docker_tag_with_compatible_api_version_rejects_tagged_base_image`, covering untagged-with-registry-port, untagged-with-localhost-port, and tagged-with-registry-port. The two "untagged" tests fail before the change and pass after it.

`uv run pytest tests/unit_tests` in `libs/cli` gives 527 passed / 3 failed; I confirmed those same 3 failures are pre-existing on unmodified `main` in my environment (Windows, Python 3.14) and are `os.linesep` CRLF assertions unrelated to this code path. `ruff check`, `ruff format --diff`, and `ty check langgraph_cli` report nothing new (the 2 `ty` diagnostics in `exec.py` are also pre-existing).

Per the external-contribution policy in `require_issue_link.yml`, could a maintainer triage this and assign it to me? I have the change and tests ready and will open the PR once assigned. Happy to adjust the approach if you'd prefer stricter reference parsing instead of the last-segment check.

title: Add support for BoRA

comments.body:
Thanks for the suggestion. BoRA looks very incremental to DoRA. As far as I can see the difference that BoRA adds a second magnitude term. I think we can re-use almost everything from DoRA including the caching (to speed up inference). It's probably best to focus on the Linear implementation first, verify correctness by running a MetaMathQA benchmark and see if the results are comparable with DoRA and then mimic the full DoRA implementation.

Would you be interested in a PR?
